sources.prompt: Thai breakfast restaurant menu board adapted from a Jira board: dynamic category columns, compact dish thumbnails, and a right-hand detail panel.
sources.screenshot: user-supplied Jira board reference (light utility shell, compact cards, column headers with counts, white detail panel on the right)

identity.oneThingToRemember: A calm, Jira-like menu board: pale utility canvas, compact white cards with small dish thumbnails, and a focused right detail panel.
identity.audience: Thai breakfast restaurant owners and front-of-house staff
identity.artDirection: flat project-management utility UI with compact density, clear dividers, category color dots, and yellow reserved for the restaurant's primary action
antiReferences: fixed scroll behavior changes in the detail panel

composition.symmetry: asymmetric dashboard shell: fixed left navigation, board center, optional right detail panel
composition.density: medium-high — 4px card radius, 8-12px board gaps, compact issue-style cards
composition.dominantAxis: horizontal board on desktop, single-column board on mobile
composition.contentWidth: full available width after the fixed 272px desktop navigation; 16-24px content gutters
composition.grid: dynamic CSS grid driven by menu categories; desktop columns can scroll horizontally, mobile columns stack
composition.whitespace: tight within cards, 12-16px between task groups and board controls
composition.focalPoint: menu board cards and the active right-hand detail panel

typography.casing: none (Thai + sentence-case English mix, as in source)
typography.contrast: high — dark navy-black text on white surface

color.accent: var(--primary-500) primary action; Mantine blue focus/selected state
usageRules: Yellow remains the product action color; category colors only identify food columns and thumbnails.
No gradients, glass, or large decorative imagery; borders and small shadows establish Jira-like hierarchy.

imagery.treatment: compact 40px thumbnail inside each board card; icon fallback until restaurant photos are uploaded
imagery.subject: dish icon from MenuItem.image, with category tint
rules: Do not turn thumbnails into large hero images.
Use the existing Phosphor SVG icon set and preserve aspect ratio.

responsive.strategy: fixed 272px left rail + flexible board/right panel on desktop; fixed mobile bar and stacked category columns below 960px
preserved: right detail panel as an in-flow sibling
allowedToChange: dynamic category columns can reduce or expand
desktop board can use horizontal overflow when detail panel is open

chatbotSurface.oneThingToRemember: A calm, Thai-first marketing assistant: warm neutral canvas, dark text, yellow identity/action cue, visible provenance, and decision cards that turn data into the next marketing question.
chatbotSurface.artDirection: content-first utility panel, flat surfaces, modest 12-16px radii, no gradients or decorative glass

usageRules: Yellow is reserved for primary send action, assistant identity, status, and list markers.
Secondary copy uses --b-700 or darker so it remains readable on --p-0 and --b-50.
Assistant and user turns use surface and yellow-tinted contrast instead of color-only role cues.

typography.body: preserve existing Mantine sm (14px) and xs (12px) sizing; use weight and spacing for hierarchy

composition.body: neutral scroll canvas with grouped turns, assistant identity row, source row, typed menu/sales/promotion cards, and recovery states
composition.composer: visible label, autosizing input, 44px send target, keyboard hint, Enter-to-send

responsive.mobile: panel becomes full width below 640px; message text keeps the existing 14px size

marketingAssistant.role: operational marketing partner for menu promotions, breakfast bundles, and draft social copy
uiBlocks: sales insight card with ranked menu items and a draft-post follow-up
menu catalogue card with configured prices and a bundle follow-up
bundle draft card with price math and owner-approval status
marketingAssistant.interaction: Cards are read-only evidence; action buttons submit a scoped follow-up question back into the same chat session.
guardrails: Prices and popularity claims come from configured restaurant data only.
Promotions and copy are drafts; the owner approves before publishing.
No auto-publish, ad spend, customer messaging, or menu-price mutations.

dashboardMobileDrawer.oneThingToRemember: Dashboard sidebar's mobile nav (< 960px) is a top-anchored, dark, height-fit-content Drawer — reuses the same slide-down pattern as the marketing navbar's mobile drawer instead of the desktop rail's left-side fixed-width panel.
dashboardMobileDrawer.prompt: iTiket screenshot reference: top bar collapses to a hamburger; tapping it slides a dark, fit-content panel down from the top edge with a brand/close header and a flat, undivided nav list.

composition.trigger: position: fixed top mobileBar (56px, top/left/right: 0, z-index 20) — brand text (no logo) + Burger, visible below 960px, replaces the desktop rail. Pinned above the page's AnnouncementBar from first paint (not just after scrolling past it, which is what position: sticky gave); .page in home/page.module.scss adds a matching 56px padding-top below 960px so the banner and shell content clear it instead of hiding underneath.
composition.panel: Mantine Drawer, position="top", size="auto" (height: fit-content), dark background, so the page stays visible below it
composition.header: brand name text only (no logo mark) + default close (X), matches navbar.tsx's mobile drawer header pattern
composition.body: SidebarContent is reused (shared with the desktop rail) but re-toned for dark + restructured for mobile: per-group section labels ("เมนูลัด", "จัดการธุรกิจ", "To-do ของฉัน") are hidden, leading icons are hidden, and all rows (to-dos + both nav groups) flow as one continuous list divided by 1px borders instead of grouped sections — matching the reference's flat list.

color.activeAccent: var(--primary-500) (text color only, no fill — reuses navbar.tsx's .mobileLinkActive convention instead of a filled highlight bar)

dashboardMobileDrawer.uxFix: Fixed a pre-existing bug surfaced by this change: the shared SidebarContent's scroll container closed the drawer (afterNavigate) on any click inside it, including the accordion expand toggle. afterNavigate is now wired only to actual <Link> clicks (top-level and child), not to the expand/collapse button.
dashboardMobileDrawer.desktopUnchanged: The >=960px persistent rail (SidebarContent inside .sidebar) keeps its section headers, icons, and light theme — only the mobile Drawer presentation changed. (Its logo/date row was later reworked — see businessCard below.)
openQuestions: Real logo asset (public/logo/init_logo.svg) was intentionally left out of the mobile drawer per explicit request — revisit if a small brand mark is wanted back in the mobile header.

businessCard.oneThingToRemember: Desktop rail's business-identity row is now the init_logo.svg wordmark + today's date — not a name/address block.
businessCard.bugFixed: The row previously rendered <Image src="/logo/cat_logo.svg" width={32} height={32} .../> using raw HTML width/height attributes. Mantine's Image component ships its own width: 100% CSS that overrides plain HTML attributes, so the logo rendered at native SVG size (huge) and blotted out the name/address text next to it. Fixed by sizing through Mantine's h/w style props instead (h={36} w="auto" fit="contain") — apply the same h/w (not width/height) convention to any future Image usage in this codebase.
businessCard.change: Replaced the cat_logo.svg + shop name + address block with /logo/init_logo.svg (h=36, w=auto, fit=contain) + a today's-date label, per explicit request ("เอา...ที่ตั้ง...เปลี่ยนทั้งหมดเป็น init_logo.svg แล้วก็วันที่"). Name/address were judged redundant here since ExpenseHeader already shows them prominently at the top of main content.
businessCard.dateFormat: Manual Thai month-name array + date.getFullYear() (Gregorian), not Intl th-TH — that locale defaults to พ.ศ. (Buddhist era) which would read inconsistently against the "2026" used elsewhere in this dashboard (e.g. the yearly expense total).
businessCard.scope: Desktop rail only (.sidebar > SidebarContent > .businessCard). The mobile Drawer already hides .businessCard entirely (see dashboardMobileDrawer above) and keeps its separate text-only brand treatment untouched.

teamPermissionMultiSelect.oneThingToRemember: Permission selectors stay visually light and keep their affordance after selection: the field is transparent, while selected values remain removable and additional permissions remain selectable.
teamPermissionMultiSelect.interaction: Show the Thai permission placeholder only while an editable member has no selected permissions; hide it after the first selection without disabling the MultiSelect input.
teamPermissionMultiSelect.surface: transparent field with the existing table surface and Mantine selected-value pills

expenseUploadPanel.oneThingToRemember: A calm, compact expense-entry side sheet: upload first, editable receipt fields second, then a clear review gate before saving.
expenseUploadPanel.artDirection: flat light utility panel with existing yellow action accent, compact bordered cards, no gradients or decorative glass

composition.desktop: 420px fixed right panel with a matching flex slot that reserves workspace width without allowing the panel to scroll away
composition.tablet: fixed right side sheet up to 460px from 960px down to 641px so the expense workspace is not squeezed
composition.flow: upload receipt → edit expense fields → review and save
composition.density: medium-high; two-column field grid, compact controls, and one body scroll region
composition.progress: compact two-step progress row with short Thai labels that stay stable at narrow widths
composition.staging: after the first upload, add-file and manual-entry actions remain available above the staged cards

interaction.upload: JPG/PNG only, max 10 MB, camera input supported
interaction.feedback: per-file scanning, success confidence, retry error, and inline rejected-file message
interaction.humanReview: OCR results with a missing unique order number, item quantity, price, date/time, or confidence below 70% cannot continue until staff marks the entry reviewed
interaction.manualFallback: manual order entry remains available when OCR is unavailable or an order slip cannot be read

expenseUploadPanel.dataContract: Panel draft and OCR response share camelCase fields via src/lib/expense/types.ts. The unique orderNumber is the only document identifier; the contract contains no expense or receipt-number fields. Mock rows retain menu lineItems for sales aggregation and add structured topping quantities/prices for order review.
expenseUploadPanel.accessibility: visible labels, role=alert for upload/OCR errors, keyboard-accessible dropzone, icon buttons labelled, reduced-motion spinner fallback

menuBoardSurface.oneThingToRemember: Menu items are scanned as board cards first; details open in a Jira-like right panel without changing the existing menu CRUD flow.

composition.board: dynamic columns from menu categories present in the catalogue; selected category filter narrows to one column
composition.card: 40px category-tinted thumbnail, two-line dish name, price, id, option count, optional best-seller badge
composition.panel: compact item header with 72px thumbnail, metadata, ingredients/options sections, sales chart, and existing edit/delete actions
composition.layoutRepair: because DashboardSidebar is fixed after the latest pull, menu content reserves 272px on desktop; SidebarShell is a full-width flex item

menuBoardSurface.panelScrollScope: Intentionally unchanged in this task; keep the current panel scroll implementation until the teammate's pull lands.

responsive.desktop: board columns stay horizontal and may scroll within the board viewport when the right detail panel is open
responsive.tablet: fixed desktop rail is replaced by the existing mobile bar at 960px
responsive.mobile: board columns stack, thumbnails stay compact, detail panel becomes full width

uxRules: Dropdown trigger is a <button> (not a link) with aria-expanded; closes on outside click and Escape.
Mobile menu toggle uses aria-expanded + aria-controls + sr-only label; body scroll locks while open.
Focus-visible outline on every interactive element.
Icons use currentColor via CSS mask so they inherit text/hover color instead of being baked-in bitmaps.
antiSlopChecks: No default purple-gradient-on-white treatment unless the source asks for it.
No invented component variants when an existing project component can be reused.
No decorative effect without a job: hierarchy, feedback, wayfinding, or brand character.
No desktop-only implementation when the brief or source implies mobile use.
No silent substitution of the source character with a generic dashboard or landing-page pattern.
openQuestions: Real logo asset and TH/EN language switcher were deferred per request — revisit when brand assets and i18n routing exist.
Nav link hrefs and dropdown items are placeholders ("#") pending real routes/IA.

analysis.notes: Existing Mantine + CSS Modules conventions are preserved. Jira reference is adapted as an operate-mode board, not a brand replacement; the menu route also compensates for the fixed dashboard rail introduced by the latest pull.

findings: Expense upload layout scan returned no mechanical findings; targeted ESLint and tsc --noEmit pass.
The production build compiled the app, but its TypeScript worker hit the environment's EPERM spawn restriction; standalone tsc --noEmit passes.

The upload panel now keeps one body scroll region, uses a compact two-step progress row, and separates a desktop width-reserving slot from the fixed viewport panel so page scrolling cannot move the form header/footer.
